title: Backup & Restore
help: pgBackRest for every cluster: how far back you can restore, backups, config on all nodes, schedule and restore.
sshHint: Used for this call only, never saved.
sshStored: Uses the cluster's saved SSH secret if left empty.
needLogin: Give the SSH login to read the nodes.
c_riskSub: Not archived yet · last WAL {{age}} ago
timelineHelp: Any moment in the blue band can be restored (point in time). Dots are backups.
label: Backup
r_latestHelp: The newest data in the repository: the last backup plus all archived WAL.
r_timeHelp: Any moment inside the recoverable window.
r_setHelp: Exactly as a backup was taken, no WAL replay after it.
r_warn: PostgreSQL is stopped on every node while it restores. Replicas are rebuilt from the same backup.
r_confirm: The current data is replaced by the restored data. Type the cluster name to confirm.
cfg_help: Edit once, write to every node of the same kind (database nodes or repository server). Each node keeps its own pg path, port and host.
cfg_keepLocal: Keep each node's own pg*-path / port / host
cfg_verify: Check after writing, put the old config back if it fails
stanzaMissing: Stanza {{stanza}} is not in the repository yet. Create it to start backups.
s_othersWarn: {{n}} other backup schedule(s) found (systemd timer or cron, not managed here). Saving adds autoNOMIC's schedule too: remove the other one to avoid double backups.
cfg_same: The config is the same on every node.
s_help: Cron on every node; only the current primary backs up, so it follows a failover.
busy: A job is running on this cluster.
noPgbackrest: No pgBackRest found. Install it on the database nodes (or a repository server) and run Discover again.
rp_help: Where backups are kept. Add a second disk or a cloud bucket for an off-site copy.
rp_addHint: Disk, S3, Azure, GCS or SFTP
rp_removeText: It is removed from the pgBackRest config on every node. The backups already stored there are not deleted.
rp_h_posixRepoHost: It is created on the repository server; the database nodes reach it through that server.
rp_h_posixShared: Every database node must see the same folder (NFS or similar), so a new primary writes there after a failover.
rp_h_cifs: A folder on a mounted Windows / CIFS share, the same on every node.
rp_h_s3: Any S3-compatible storage: AWS S3, MinIO, Ceph, Wasabi… Every node writes to it directly.
rp_h_azure: An Azure Blob Storage container. Every node writes to it directly.
rp_h_gcs: A Google Cloud Storage bucket. The key file must be on every node (or use the machine's own account).
rp_h_sftp: A folder on an SFTP server. The private key file must be on every node.
rp_retentionHelp: Older ones are removed after a new full backup.
rp_cipherHelp: Optional. Keep it safe: without it the backups cannot be read.
rp_safe: Written on every node, then the stanza is created and checked there. If that fails, every node is put back as it was. Keys never leave the nodes.
rn_finished: The running backup finished. Status refreshed.
